result.title: 3 Top Finance Stories & CEO Gender Gap| WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - This colourful school is also a power plant:
Today, any building can become a renewable power plant. This design approach is called building-integrated photovoltaics - and it could turn the world’s built environment into a vast clean energy resource. Here are 3 striking examples.

01:55 - The top finance stories you need to know:
Global finance is being tested. Digital editor Spencer Feingold breaks down the latest developments being tracked by the World Economic Forum's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems.

03:27 - Fewer than a third of the world’s CEOs are women, UN data shows:
Women hold just 31% of #management positions worldwide, according to a new survey by the ILO. This is despite the fact that businesses led by a female #CEO are 6% more likely to report higher profits - while those with a female chair are 18% more likely.

04:53 - This new glue could make batteries greener:
Recycling lithium batteries could one day be as simple as soaking them in water. Researchers at UC San Diego have developed a new water-soluble glue that could make #lithium batteries easier to recycle - without compromising performance.

result.title: We all depend on the construction industry. Here’s why it urgently needs more workers
result.description:
Ebru Özdemir, chair of infrastructure company Limak, explains why ‘maker skills’ are becoming ever more vital to the 21st-century economy.

‘Maker skills’ are the practical abilities that power the physical economy, from constructing and installing to operating equipment and processing materials. Demand for them is rising faster than supply. The World Economic Forum’s The First Mile Sandbox aims to foster talent pipelines by connecting universities with employers and other stakeholders.

result.title: What’s Next for Chief Sustainability Officers? 3 Top Leaders Explain
result.description:
Sustainability is moving out of the strategy deck and into the operating plan. In this episode, chief sustainability officers from Ant Group, Heidelberg Materials and Mastercard explain how the profession is evolving - and how it has navigated a challenging environment beset by geopolitical uncertainty, shifting regulation, infrastructure gaps and pressure to prove measurable business value. In this special collection episode, leaders put the moment in context while sharing top trends and insights from the recent World Economic Forum Chief Sustainability Officer’s Outlook.

Top topics:
- Momentum for sustainability hasn’t stalled - just fragmented.
- Why progress has come where sustainability has a strong business case
- How the CSO role could change for ‘best run’ companies in a decade
- Key messages these leaders share for COP31 leaders

Leaders in this episode:
Sabrina Peng, Chief Sustainability Officer, Ant Group
Ellen Jackowski, Chief Sustainability Officer, Mastercard
Katharina Beumelburg, Chief Sustainability Officer, Heidelberg Materials

This episode of Meet The Leader was recorded in New York during UN General Assembly week during the World Economic Forum’s Sustainability Development Meetings.

result.title: 3 things to know about finance right now
result.description:
Global finance is being tested.

The world needs an estimated $56 trillion to finance major challenges, from clean energy and AI to national defence. At the same time, volatile AI stocks and new IPOs are prompting fresh questions about expected returns and high valuations.

Meanwhile, digital assets are moving from the margins of finance into the mainstream. As new forms of ownership and cross-border payments develop, regulators face a pressing question: can the rules keep pace?

Digital editor Spencer Feingold breaks down the latest developments being tracked by the World Economic Forum's Centre for Financial and Monetary Systems.

result.title: Fewer than a third of the world’s CEOs are women, UN data shows
result.description:
Women hold just 31% of #management positions worldwide, according to a new survey by the @ILO.

This is despite the fact that businesses led by a female #CEO are 6% more likely to report higher profits - while those with a female chair are 18% more likely.

The Global Gender Gap Report 2026 charts a significant ‘drop to the top’: while 46% of entry-level workers are #women, just 23% of those in the C-suite are women.
